Reproducing Russo, Claar, Furregoni et al. (2025) from dandiset 000458¶

Paper. Russo S, Claar LD, Furregoni G, Marks LC, Krishnan G, Zauli FM, et al., Koch C, Rembado I (2025). Thalamic feedback shapes brain responses evoked by cortical stimulation in mice and humans. Nature Communications 16:3627. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-58717-2. The claims file (claims/russo-2025.yaml) was written from the version of record in PubMed Central, with the supplement and the Source Data file.

Dandiset. DANDI:000458, version 0.230317.0039 (Claar et al. 2023, "Simultaneous electroencephalography, extracellular electrophysiology, and cortical electrical stimulation in head-fixed mice"). This is the version the paper's Data availability statement cites, and the only published version. The draft has the same 24 assets and size and lists 10 active uploads; it was not used.

What the dandiset holds. 24 sessions from 23 mice, each with 30-channel EEG, the LFP of up to three Neuropixels probes, sorted units, wheel speed and a trial table, in an awake, an isoflurane and sometimes a recovery epoch. Ten sessions (ten mice) have deep MOs stimulation while awake, nine of them with probes; these are the mouse data used here. The paper reports 26 EEG sessions from 15 mice and units from 21 mice, so the dandiset holds part of them. No session has stimulation of the posterior control areas of Figure S6.

Outside inputs. The human claims are tested on the paper's Source Data file (41467_2025_58717_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx from the publisher's site, checked by SHA-256), which is also the reference for the link claim. The optogenetic claims are in the second notebook, opto_russo_2025.ipynb, on the paper's figshare deposit (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.28440311.v1).

Running. The helper russo.py streams the needed chunks of each file from the archive in parallel; the notebook takes about 15 minutes, nearly all of it reading the EEG and the MOs LFP of the ten sessions. The model section fetches and builds the paper's network model, which needs make and g++.

    """Seed of a claim's generator (docs/protocol.md, Author, step 3)."""
    return zlib.crc32(f"russo-2025/{claim}".encode())

The trial tables hold electrical stimulation of MOs (deep and superficial) and of SSp (deep and superficial). No file has a stimulation target in visual or retrosplenial cortex or hippocampus, the control sessions of Figure S6. The paper's mouse results use deep MOs stimulation (Results: "targeting the deep layers of MOs (layer 5/6...)"); ten sessions from ten mice have it, nine of them with Neuropixels probes and units. The paper reports 26 EEG sessions from 15 mice (Figure 1C) and units from 21 mice (Figure S7B), so the dandiset holds part of its mouse data.

Every session has 120 trials at each of three currents, as the Methods state (up to 120 pulses per intensity). The currents of this subset (printed above) are close to the paper's means. Wheel speed is in cm/s and ranges from 0 to tens of cm/s. The file's is_running is defined as a mean speed above 0 cm/s; the agreement column shows it matches the mean speed from -0.5 to +0.5 s computed here from the running_speed series, which is consistent with the trial times and the speed sharing a clock (both come from the same pipeline, so this does not prove it). The paper's threshold is 0.1 cm/s, used below.

Clock of the signals: the onset of each trial falls within one sample (0.4 ms) of an EEG and LFP timestamp, and the stimulation artifact in the raw trial-averaged EEG and LFP sits within one sample of the onset in every session (columns *_artifact_lag_ms), so the EEG, the LFP and the trial table share a clock.

# Spike clock: population response of responsive MOs RS units in 2-10 ms against the same window
# of onsets shifted by +1.7 s (between pulses, 3.5-4.5 s apart).
rows = []
for r in S.values():
    if not r.get("has_probes"):
        continue
    t = r["trials"]
    hi = (t.intensity == "high").to_numpy()
    on, sh = [], []
    for i, (rel, trial) in r["spikes"].items():
        if r["units"].loc[i, "cls"] not in ("RS", "relay"):
            continue
        sel = hi[trial]
        on.append(((rel[sel] >= 0.002) & (rel[sel] < 0.010)).sum() / hi.sum() / 0.008)
        sh.append(((rel[sel] >= -0.3) & (rel[sel] < -0.292)).sum() / hi.sum() / 0.008)
    rows.append({"subject": r["subject"], "units": len(on), "rate_2_10ms": np.mean(on), "rate_-300_-292ms": np.mean(sh)})
print("\nMean rate of RS and relay units in 2-10 ms after the pulse and in an 8 ms window 300 ms before it (Hz):")
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(2).to_string(index=False))

waveform_duration is described in the files as seconds; its values (0.110 to 2.074, cell above) are milliseconds, and are read as such. The spiking rate in the 2 to 10 ms after the pulse is far above the rate in a window of equal length before it in every mouse, so the units and the trial times share a clock. Unit analyses use the trials the file marks valid (is_valid); the paper removed bad trials using a lab spreadsheet that is not public.

def state_table(sig, intens=("high",), thr=0.1, chan="all", win="late", meas="amp"):
    """One row per session and intensity: the measure at rest and during running."""
    rows = []
    for r in S.values():
        if sig not in r:
            continue
        d = r[sig]
        d = d[(d.threshold == thr) & (d.chan == chan) & (d.window == win) & d.intensity.isin(intens)]
        for i, g in d.groupby("intensity"):
            g = g.set_index("state")
            rows.append({"subject": r["subject"], "intensity": i, "rest": g.loc["rest", meas],
                         "active": g.loc["active", meas], "n_rest": int(g.loc["rest", "n"]),
                         "n_active": int(g.loc["active", "n"])})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def signed_rank(t, label, by_mouse=False):
    t = t.dropna(subset=["rest", "active"])
    if by_mouse:
        t = t.groupby("subject")[["rest", "active"]].mean().reset_index()
    w = stats.wilcoxon(t.rest, t.active) if len(t) > 1 else None
    return {"reading": label, "n": len(t), "rest_median": t.rest.median(), "active_median": t.active.median(),
            "rest_larger": int((t.rest > t.active).sum()), "p": (w.pvalue if w else np.nan),
            "effect_median_diff": (t.rest - t.active).median()}


READINGS = {"(a)(i) high, all channels and trials": (("high",), "all"),
            "(a)(ii) high, valid channels and trials": (("high",), "valid"),
            "(b)(i) high and medium, all": (("high", "medium"), "all"),
            "(b)(ii) high and medium, valid": (("high", "medium"), "valid")}


def readings_table(sig, meas="amp", win="late", thr=0.1, by_mouse_b=False):
    out = []
    for label, (intens, chan) in READINGS.items():
        t = state_table(sig, intens, thr, chan, win, meas)
        out.append(signed_rank(t, label))
        if by_mouse_b and len(intens) == 2:
            out.append(signed_rank(t, label + ", mean per mouse", by_mouse=True))
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

In mice, the late (150 to 250 ms) EEG response to deep MOs electrical stimulation has a larger rectified amplitude at rest than during running.

Rectified amplitude: the absolute value of the trial-averaged EP from 150 to 250 ms, averaged over time and EEG channels; two-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank test pairing rest and active per session (criterion). Readings as the criterion lists them: (a) high intensity only, (b) high and medium as separate sessions; (i) all channels and trials, (ii) the channels (is_data_valid) and trials (is_valid) the file flags as good. The code's measure (mean absolute single-trial signal after baseline z-scoring) is a variant.

Left panel range: 5.0 to 211.9 uV over -100 to 400 ms

**Result: reproduced. The late EEG rectified amplitude is larger at rest than during running in all 10 sessions at high intensity (median 81.7 against 42.6 uV, two-tailed signed-rank p = 0.00195), and the test gives p < 0.05 with rest larger under all four readings (p = 0.00195 for both channel and trial selections at high intensity, p = 4e-06 with high and medium as 20 sessions). The code's z-scored single-trial measure agrees (p = 0.0039 and 4e-06). Ten sessions from ten mice are used, where the paper reports 26 sessions from 15 mice.

speed-threshold-robust¶

The EEG, LFP and CSD state modulations remain when the speed threshold separating rest and active trials is raised up to 5 cm/s.

Thresholds 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 cm/s (criterion's grid), reading (a)(i) of the base claims (high intensity, all channels and trials), and the same with the file's valid channels and trials. A session enters at a threshold when it has at least one trial in each state; at least 10 per state is a variant. The file's own is_running (above 0 cm/s) is shown as well.

In [12]:
rows = []
for sig in ["eeg", "lfp", "csd"]:
    for chan in ["all", "valid"]:
        for thr in russo.THRESHOLDS + ["file"]:
            t = state_table(sig, ("high",), thr, chan)
            t = t[(t.n_rest >= 1) & (t.n_active >= 1)]
            t10 = t[(t.n_rest >= 10) & (t.n_active >= 10)]
            a, b = signed_rank(t, ""), signed_rank(t10, "")
            rows.append({"signal": sig, "chan": chan, "threshold": thr, "n": a["n"], "rest_larger": a["rest_larger"],
                         "p": a["p"], "n_min10": b["n"], "p_min10": b["p"]})
res_thr = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(res_thr.round(6).to_string(index=False))

# The criterion as written: at each threshold of the grid, EEG, LFP and CSD give p < 0.05 with rest larger
# (reading (a)(i), all channels and trials, sessions with at least one trial per state)
grid = res_thr[(res_thr.chan == "all") & res_thr.threshold.isin(russo.THRESHOLDS)].copy()
grid["passes"] = (grid.p < 0.05) & (grid.rest_larger > grid.n / 2)
print("\nCriterion, p < 0.05 with rest larger:")
print(grid.pivot(index="threshold", columns="signal", values="passes").to_string())
print(f"All three signals at every threshold: {bool(grid.passes.all())}")

Result: not reproduced. The EEG modulation holds at every threshold from 0.1 to 5 cm/s (10 of 10 sessions, p = 0.00195 each). The LFP holds up to 2 cm/s (p = 0.039) and not at 5 cm/s (p = 0.098). The CSD holds only at 0.1 cm/s (p = 0.0195); from 0.5 cm/s on p = 0.074 to 0.36, with rest larger in 7 of 9 mice throughout. The criterion asks for EEG, LFP and CSD at every threshold and has no clause for a partial result, so the failures of LFP and CSD in the check above make the claim not reproduced, by the same rule as fig3e-lf-synchrony-reduced. With at least 10 trials per state the EEG also loses significance at 5 cm/s (5 sessions, p = 0.0625). This outcome was proposed after the second verification round and agreed by the third.

The early LFP amplitude is larger during running (rest larger in 2 of 9 mice, p = 0.0195; reading (b) 5 of 18, p = 0.0013). The early CSD differs at p = 0.048 with high and medium (rest larger in 12 of 18, medians 1.85 and 1.87) but not at high alone (p = 0.055), so the CSD part holds under reading (b) only.

triphasic-pattern¶

Deep MOs stimulation evokes a triphasic spiking pattern in MOs and SM-TH, an initial excitation within 10 ms, an off period of about 10 to 140 ms (127.8 +- 4.1 ms of silence) and a rebound excitation at 140 to 250 ms.

Population PSTH (1 ms bins) of responsive RS units in MOs and relay units in SM-TH at high intensity, per mouse. Readings of the silence (criterion): (a) per mouse, the median over units of the first-spike latency in 75 to 250 ms minus 10 ms, averaged over mice; (b) per mouse, the time the population rate stays below its baseline mean minus 2 SD after the initial peak.

In [14]:
def psth_shape(r, cls):
    c, rate, n = russo.population_psth(r, cls)
    if rate is None:
        return None
    base = rate[(c >= -0.5) & (c < -0.05)]
    mu, sd = base.mean(), base.std()
    init = rate[(c >= 0.002) & (c < 0.010)]
    off = rate[(c >= 0.010) & (c < 0.140)]
    reb = rate[(c >= 0.140) & (c < 0.250)]
    # reading (b): from the end of the initial peak (first bin after 2 ms back under the mean), time below mu - 2 SD
    k0 = np.searchsorted(c, 0.010)
    below = rate < mu - 2 * sd
    k = k0
    while k < len(rate) and not below[k] and c[k] < 0.05:
        k += 1
    start = k
    while k < len(rate) and (below[k] or np.all(below[k:k + 3])):
        k += 1
    silence_b = (c[k] - c[start]) * 1e3 if start < len(rate) and below[start] else 0.0
    return {"units": n, "baseline_Hz": mu, "initial_peak_Hz": init.max(), "initial_peak_ms": c[(c >= 0.002) & (c < 0.010)][init.argmax()] * 1e3,
            "frac_10_140_below_baseline": float((off < mu).mean()), "rebound_peak_Hz": reb.max(),
            "rebound_peak_ms": c[(c >= 0.140) & (c < 0.250)][reb.argmax()] * 1e3, "silence_b_ms": silence_b}

def silence_b(c, rate, smooth_ms):
    """Reading (b) on the PSTH smoothed by a running mean over smooth_ms 1 ms bins: from the first bin
    after 10 ms below the baseline mean minus 2 SD (baseline -500 to -50 ms of the smoothed PSTH),
    the time until it comes back above."""
    sm = np.convolve(rate, np.ones(smooth_ms) / smooth_ms, "same") if smooth_ms > 1 else rate
    base = sm[(c >= -0.5) & (c < -0.05)]
    mu, sd = base.mean(), base.std()
    below = sm < mu - 2 * sd
    k = np.searchsorted(c, 0.010)
    while k < len(sm) and not below[k] and c[k] < 0.05:
        k += 1
    if k >= len(sm) or not below[k]:
        return mu, sd, 0.0
    start = k
    while k < len(sm) and below[k]:
        k += 1
    return mu, sd, (c[k] - c[start]) * 1e3


SMOOTH = [1, 2, 5, 10, 20]

            row[f"silence_{k}ms"] = s

Result: partially reproduced. The triphasic pattern is present in every mouse: the initial peak falls at 2.5 to 9.5 ms, the rate is below baseline over a mean of 99% (RS) and 88% (relay) of 10 to 140 ms, and the rebound peaks at 150 to 194 ms. The silence does not match 127.8 +- 4.1 ms under either reading of the criterion: (a) 171.5 ms (RS) and 160.8 ms (relay), (b) 57.9 and 71.4 ms. Reading (b) on 1 ms bins is degenerate: with baseline rates of 2.6 to 8.8 Hz the threshold, baseline mean minus 2 SD, is 0.05 to 6.51 Hz and below zero for the one-unit relay population of 551399, and 7 of the 16 populations give silences of 0 to 5 ms. On PSTHs smoothed by a running mean, the RS silence is 113.8 ms (2 ms), 134.1 (5 ms), 132.8 (10 ms) and 127.9 ms (20 ms), within 123.7 to 131.9 ms only at 20 ms; the relay silence stays at 86.4 to 98.7 ms (100.8 to 107.3 ms without 551399). So the RS value comes near the paper's at wider smoothing, and the relay value does not at any width.

fig2b-thalamus-leads¶

The late rebound of SM-TH units precedes that of MOs RS units and the late CSD, LFP and EEG peaks, at rest and during running.

Per mouse at high intensity (criterion): SM-TH and MOs latency, per trial the median over responsive relay (SM-TH) or RS (MOs) units of the first-spike latency in 75 to 250 ms, averaged over trials; EEG, LFP and CSD latency, per trial the largest GFP peak in 75 to 250 ms whose prominence exceeds the baseline mean plus 3 SD, averaged over trials. Two-way ANOVA on measure and state, Tukey HSD on the measure. Tukey within each state is shown as well.

def trial_unit_latency(cls, col="lat_reb", frame=H):
    """Per mouse and trial, the median over the class's responsive units of the latency."""
    return frame[frame.cls == cls].groupby(["subject", "trial"])[col].median()


rows = []
for r in S.values():
    if not r.get("has_probes"):
        continue
    t = r["trials"]
    hi = (t.intensity == "high") & t.is_valid
    per = {"EEG": pd.Series(r["eeg_lat"]), "LFP": pd.Series(r["lfp_lat"]), "CSD": pd.Series(r["csd_lat"])}
    for name, cls in [("SM-TH", "relay"), ("MOs", "RS")]:
        s = trial_unit_latency(cls)
        if r["subject"] in s.index.get_level_values(0):
            per[name] = s.loc[r["subject"]].reindex(range(len(t)))
    for name, lat in per.items():
        for st, m in [("rest", hi & ~t.active), ("active", hi & t.active)]:
            v = lat[m.to_numpy()].dropna()
            if len(v):
                rows.append({"subject": r["subject"], "measure": name, "state": st, "latency": v.mean(), "trials": len(v)})

Result: not reproduced. The measure factor of the two-way ANOVA is not significant (F = 1.41, p = 0.24) and no Tukey comparison of SM-TH with another measure is (adjusted p 0.29 to 0.84). SM-TH has the shortest mean latency during running (146.4 ms against 158.0 to 163.3 for the others) but not at rest (173.4 against 172.3 to 176.1). With the EEG and LFP GFP over the valid channels only, the measure factor gives p = 0.38 and the Tukey comparisons of SM-TH adjusted p 0.57 to 0.83. Only 7 mice have responsive relay units, against 20 in the paper.

fig3a-thalamic-rate-higher-active¶

The evoked firing rate of SM-TH units in the late window (150 to 250 ms) is higher during running than at rest, unlike the late EP component.

Responsive relay units at high intensity; per unit and trial, spikes in 150 to 250 ms over 0.1 s. Readings (criterion): (a) per unit, signed-rank on unit pairs; (b) per mouse, the median over its units, signed-rank; (c) per trial, the mean over the session's units, rank-sum on rest against active trials pooled over sessions. Variant: the code's rank-sum on per-session medians. As the sessions differ in rate and in their fractions of active trials, reading (c) is also shown within each session and as a session-stratified rank-sum (van Elteren); these are checks, not readings of the criterion.

In [20]:
def rate_readings(cls, frame=H, col="rate_late"):
    d = frame[frame.cls == cls]
    pu = d.groupby(["subject", "unit", "active"])[col].mean().unstack().dropna()
    pm = pu.groupby("subject").median()
    pt = d.groupby(["subject", "trial", "active"])[col].mean().reset_index()
    out = []
    w = stats.wilcoxon(pu[False], pu[True])
    out.append({"reading": "(a) per unit, signed-rank", "n": len(pu), "rest": pu[False].mean(), "active": pu[True].mean(), "p": w.pvalue})
    if len(pm) > 1:
        w = stats.wilcoxon(pm[False], pm[True])
        out.append({"reading": "(b) per mouse median, signed-rank", "n": len(pm), "rest": pm[False].median(), "active": pm[True].median(), "p": w.pvalue})
    a, rr = pt[pt.active][col], pt[~pt.active][col]
    out.append({"reading": "(c) per trial, rank-sum", "n": f"{len(rr)} rest, {len(a)} active", "rest": rr.mean(), "active": a.mean(),
                "p": stats.mannwhitneyu(rr, a).pvalue})
    sm = d.groupby(["subject", "active"])[col].median().unstack()
    out.append({"reading": "code variant, per-session medians, rank-sum", "n": len(sm), "rest": sm[False].median(), "active": sm[True].median(),
                "p": stats.mannwhitneyu(sm[False].dropna(), sm[True].dropna()).pvalue})
    return pd.DataFrame(out), pu

def van_elteren(d, col):
    """Session-stratified rank-sum test (van Elteren 1960): rest against active trials within each
    session, rank sums weighted by 1/(n+1), normal approximation with the tie correction."""
    num, var = 0.0, 0.0
    for _, s in d.groupby("subject"):
        a, r = s[s.active][col].to_numpy(), s[~s.active][col].to_numpy()
        if len(a) == 0 or len(r) == 0:
            continue
        n = len(a) + len(r)
        ranks = stats.rankdata(np.r_[a, r])
        _, cnt = np.unique(np.r_[a, r], return_counts=True)
        v = len(a) * len(r) / 12 * ((n + 1) - (cnt ** 3 - cnt).sum() / (n * (n - 1)))
        w = 1 / (n + 1)
        num += w * (ranks[:len(a)].sum() - len(a) * (n + 1) / 2)
        var += w ** 2 * v
    z = num / np.sqrt(var)
    return z, 2 * stats.norm.sf(abs(z))


def per_session_rates(cls, frame=H, col="rate_late"):
    """Reading (c) within each session: per trial the mean over the session's units, rest against active."""
    d = frame[frame.cls == cls]
    pt = d.groupby(["subject", "trial", "active"])[col].mean().reset_index()
    rows = []
    for s, g in pt.groupby("subject"):
        a, r = g[g.active][col], g[~g.active][col]
        rows.append({"subject": s, "units": d[d.subject == s].unit.nunique(), "trials_rest": len(r), "trials_active": len(a),
                     "rest_Hz": r.mean(), "active_Hz": a.mean(),
                     "p_ranksum": stats.mannwhitneyu(r, a).pvalue if len(a) and len(r) else np.nan})
    z, p = van_elteren(pt, col)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), z, p

Result: reproduced, under reading (c) only. Per trial, the mean late rate of responsive relay units is higher during running (17.2 against 13.9 Hz; rank-sum p = 0.00054, 681 rest and 150 active trials). Per unit (303 units, 14.8 against 14.4 Hz, p = 0.41) and per mouse (7 mice, p = 0.30) the difference is not significant, nor with the code's per-session medians (p = 0.24). The pooled per-trial test mixes sessions with different rates and fractions of active trials. Within sessions the rate is higher during running in 5 of 7 (significantly in 4: 551399, 569068, 569073, 571619) and significantly lower in 551397 (17.3 against 13.5 Hz); the session-stratified van Elteren test gives p = 0.19. The criterion accepts reading (c), so the outcome stands, but it does not hold within sessions taken together.

Result: reproduced, by the criterion, which fixes the test as the per-trial reading (c) adopted for fig3a-thalamic-rate-higher-active: neither FS (22.1 against 20.3 Hz, p = 0.35) nor TRN (31.2 against 30.3 Hz, p = 0.88) differs by state (table above). This outcome was proposed after the second verification round and agreed by the third. It is fragile on two counts.

First, FS rates are lower during running per unit and per mouse (p = 0.0068 and 0.039), and within sessions they are lower in 6 of 8 (significantly in 5), with van Elteren p = 1.3e-08; in 569069 they are significantly higher during running (27.6 against 22.8 Hz, p = 0.0033). The pooled test hides this because the sessions differ in rate and in their fractions of active trials, as for fig3a (van Elteren p = 0.19).

Second, the outcome depends on TRN being the SM-TH units under 0.35 ms. Adding the one responsive RT unit (546655) to TRN makes the pooled per-trial TRN test significant (30.3 against 22.0 Hz, p = 8e-06), which would make the claim not reproduced. This comes from the same mixing (that session has 81 of 119 trials active); stratified by session it gives p = 0.77, and per unit and per mouse p = 0.47 and 0.69. TRN on the SM-TH class does not differ under any reading (p = 0.31 to 1) nor within sessions (van Elteren p = 0.39).

fig3b-bimodal-isi¶

The evoked late ISI of putative thalamic relay units is bimodal, splitting them into high-firing (HF, ISI below 17.88 ms, 569 units) and low-firing (LF, 700 units) groups, while the ISI distributions of cortical RS, cortical FS and TRN units are unimodal.

Evoked ISI per unit: the median over trials of the interval between the first spike and the next in the window, (a) 150 to 250 ms (Methods) or (b) 75 to 250 ms (code). k-means with two clusters on the log ISI of the relay units, seeded from the claim; threshold the largest ISI of the short cluster. Hartigan's dip test on log10 ISI per class, with the diptest package (tabulated p-values); the paper's code used unidip, which does not run with current numpy.

In [25]:
SEED_3B = claim_seed("fig3b-bimodal-isi")


def isi_split(col, seed):
    isi = H.groupby(["subject", "unit", "cls"])[col].median().dropna().reset_index()
    rel = isi[isi.cls == "relay"].copy()
    km = KMeans(2, n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(np.log(rel[col].to_numpy() * 1e3).reshape(-1, 1))
    short = int(np.argmin(km.cluster_centers_.ravel()))
    rel["group"] = np.where(km.labels_ == short, "HF", "LF")
    thr = rel.loc[rel.group == "HF", col].max() * 1e3
    return isi, rel, thr


res3b = {}
for label, col in [("(a) 150-250 ms", "isi_late"), ("(b) 75-250 ms", "isi_reb")]:
    isi, rel, thr = isi_split(col, SEED_3B)
    res3b[label] = (isi, rel, thr)
    dips = {c: diptest.diptest(np.log10(isi[isi.cls == c][col].to_numpy() * 1e3)) for c in ["relay", "TRN", "RS", "FS"]}
    print(f"{label}: units per class {isi.groupby('cls').size().to_dict()}")
    print(f"  k-means: HF {int((rel.group == 'HF').sum())}, LF {int((rel.group == 'LF').sum())}, threshold {thr:.2f} ms")
    print("  dip test (dip, p):", {c: (round(d, 4), round(p, 4)) for c, (d, p) in dips.items()})
    print("  relay ISI percentiles 5, 25, 50, 75, 95 (ms):", np.round(np.percentile(rel[col] * 1e3, [5, 25, 50, 75, 95]), 2))
    print(f"  relay units with ISI above 17.88 ms: {int((rel[col] * 1e3 > 17.88).sum())} of {len(rel)}")
    seeds = []
    for k in range(5):
        _, rk, tk_ = isi_split(col, SEED_3B + 1000 * k)
        seeds.append((int((rk.group == "HF").sum()), round(tk_, 2)))
    print("  HF count and threshold under seeds +0, +1000, ..., +4000:", seeds)

Result: not reproduced. The evoked ISI of the 296 relay units is not bimodal (dip test p = 0.73 for 150 to 250 ms, 0.64 for 75 to 250 ms); the median is 2.6 ms and only 8 units have an ISI above 17.88 ms. k-means splits off a small long-ISI group (HF 278, LF 18, threshold 6.9 ms; 281, 15 and 7.5 ms in the wider window). TRN, RS and FS are unimodal (p = 0.15 to 0.95), and TRN with the RT unit too (p = 0.80 and 0.18). The counts and threshold under the four other seeds are 277 to 281 and 6.6 to 7.5 ms. Every HF and LF claim below is tested on these groups: an LF group of 18 units (8 with the 17.88 ms threshold) from 4 mice, against 700 LF units in the paper.

def hf_lf_groups(split):
    if split == "k-means (a)":
        rel = res3b["(a) 150-250 ms"][1]
        return rel.set_index(["subject", "unit"]).group
    rel = res3b["(a) 150-250 ms"][1].copy()
    rel["group"] = np.where(rel.isi_late * 1e3 < 17.88, "HF", "LF")
    return rel.set_index(["subject", "unit"]).group

fig3e-baseline-rate-doubles¶

During running the baseline firing rate of thalamic relay units almost doubles (6.78 +- 4.4 Hz at rest, 12.48 +- 4.6 Hz active), for both HF and LF units.

Baseline rate per unit and trial: spikes in -1 to -0.01 s over 0.99 s, responsive relay units at high intensity, HF and LF as split in fig3b-bimodal-isi (k-means, reading (a)); the 17.88 ms threshold is a variant. Readings (criterion): (a) per trial, the mean over the group's units, rest against active trials pooled over sessions, rank-sum, Bonferroni over HF and LF; the mean and SD are over the HF and LF trial values pooled; (b) per unit, mean over rest and active trials, signed-rank.

In [29]:
def grouped(split):
    g = hf_lf_groups(split).rename("group")
    return H[H.cls == "relay"].join(g, on=["subject", "unit"], how="inner")


def per_trial(df, func):
    """Per session, trial and group: a value over the group's units in that trial."""
    return df.groupby(["subject", "trial", "group", "active"]).apply(func).rename("v").dropna().reset_index()


def feature_tests(pt, pu=None, bonf=2):
    rows = []
    for grp in ["HF", "LF"]:
        d = pt[pt.group == grp]
        rest, act = d[~d.active].v, d[d.active].v
        p = stats.mannwhitneyu(rest, act).pvalue if len(rest) and len(act) else np.nan
        row = {"group": grp, "trials_rest": len(rest), "trials_active": len(act), "rest_mean": rest.mean(), "rest_sd": rest.std(),
               "active_mean": act.mean(), "active_sd": act.std(), "p_ranksum_trials_bonf": min(1, p * bonf)}
        if pu is not None:
            u = pu[pu.group == grp]
            w = stats.wilcoxon(u[False], u[True]) if len(u) > 1 else None
            row.update({"units_or_mice": len(u), "rest_med_b": u[False].median(), "active_med_b": u[True].median(),
                        "p_signedrank_b_bonf": min(1, w.pvalue * bonf) if w else np.nan})
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


for split in ["k-means (a)", "17.88 ms"]:
    G = grouped(split)
    pt = per_trial(G, lambda d: d.rate_base.mean())
    pu = G.groupby(["group", "subject", "unit", "active"]).rate_base.mean().unstack().dropna().reset_index()
    print(f"HF/LF split: {split}")
    print(feature_tests(pt, pu).round(5).to_string(index=False))
    both = pt.groupby("active").v.agg(["mean", "std", "size"])
    print("HF and LF trial values pooled (Hz): rest %.2f +- %.2f (n %d), active %.2f +- %.2f (n %d); paper 6.78 +- 4.4 and 12.48 +- 4.6"
          % (both.loc[False, "mean"], both.loc[False, "std"], both.loc[False, "size"], both.loc[True, "mean"], both.loc[True, "std"], both.loc[True, "size"]))
    allu = per_trial(H[H.cls == "relay"].assign(group="all"), lambda d: d.rate_base.mean())
    print("All responsive relay units, per trial (Hz): rest %.2f, active %.2f\n" % (allu[~allu.active].v.mean(), allu[allu.active].v.mean()))

fig3e-lf-synchrony-reduced¶

During running the rebound onset variability (ROV) of LF units increases (35.7 +- 11.8 to 40.7 +- 8.2 ms), a loss of synchrony, while the ROV of HF units does not change.

ROV per trial: the SD across the group's units of the first-spike latency, in (a) 150 to 250 ms (Methods) or (b) 75 to 250 ms (code); trials with at least two units firing. Unit of test (criterion): per trial, rank-sum (Bonferroni over HF and LF); per mouse, the mean ROV of its rest and active trials, signed-rank.

figs13-thalamic-features-predict-eeg¶

On single trials, baseline thalamic rate predicts HF response frequency and LF onset variability, and the late EEG amplitude is predicted by ROV of HF and LF units and by HF response frequency, but not by LF response frequency.

Per trial at high intensity: the HF and LF features of the two claims above (window (a), k-means split), the group's baseline rate, and the single-trial EEG late amplitude (mean over valid channels of |EEG| in 150 to 250 ms). Models from the Methods with statsmodels mixedlm; readings (a) raw values, (b) the code's transforms (log of the EEG amplitude and of the frequencies, every term centred).

G = grouped("k-means (a)")
feat = {}
for grp in ["HF", "LF"]:
    d = G[G.group == grp]
    gb = d.groupby(["subject", "trial"])
    feat[f"Base{grp}"] = gb.rate_base.mean()
    feat[f"ROV{grp}"] = gb.lat_late.apply(lambda x: x.std() * 1e3 if x.notna().sum() >= 2 else np.nan)
    feat[f"Freq{grp}"] = gb.isi_late.apply(lambda x: 1.0 / x.median() if x.notna().any() else np.nan)
F13 = pd.DataFrame(feat)
eeg_amp = pd.concat({r["subject"]: pd.Series(r["eeg_single_late"]) for r in S.values()}, names=["subject", "trial"])
F13["EEG"] = eeg_amp.reindex(F13.index)
F13 = F13.reset_index()


def fit13(df, formula, transform):
    d = df.copy()
    if transform:
        for c in ["EEG", "FreqHF", "FreqLF"]:
            if c in d:
                d[c] = np.log(d[c])
        for c in d.columns:
            if c not in ("subject", "trial"):
                d[c] = d[c] - d[c].mean()
    return smf.mixedlm(formula, d, groups=d["subject"]).fit()


rows = []
expect = {("ROVHF", "BaseHF"): False, ("FreqHF", "BaseHF"): True, ("ROVLF", "BaseLF"): True, ("FreqLF", "BaseLF"): False,
          ("EEG", "ROVHF"): True, ("EEG", "FreqHF"): True, ("EEG", "ROVLF"): True, ("EEG", "FreqLF"): False}
for transform in [False, True]:
    for y, x in [("ROVHF", "BaseHF"), ("FreqHF", "BaseHF"), ("ROVLF", "BaseLF"), ("FreqLF", "BaseLF")]:
        d = F13.dropna(subset=[y, x])
        f = fit13(d[["subject", "trial", y, x]], f"{y} ~ {x}", transform)
        rows.append({"reading": "(b) code transforms" if transform else "(a) raw", "model": f"{y} ~ {x}", "term": x, "trials": len(d),
                     "mice": d.subject.nunique(), "coef": f.params[x], "p": f.pvalues[x], "paper_significant": expect[(y, x)]})
    d = F13.dropna(subset=["EEG", "ROVHF", "FreqHF", "ROVLF", "FreqLF"])
    if len(d) > 10 and d.subject.nunique() > 1:
        f = fit13(d[["subject", "trial", "EEG", "FreqHF", "ROVHF", "FreqLF", "ROVLF"]], "EEG ~ FreqHF + ROVHF + FreqLF + ROVLF", transform)
        for x in ["ROVHF", "FreqHF", "ROVLF", "FreqLF"]:
            rows.append({"reading": "(b) code transforms" if transform else "(a) raw", "model": "EEG ~ FreqHF + ROVHF + FreqLF + ROVLF", "term": x,
                         "trials": len(d), "mice": d.subject.nunique(), "coef": f.params[x], "p": f.pvalues[x], "paper_significant": expect[("EEG", x)]})
    else:
        print(f"EEG model not fitted: {len(d)} trials with all four features from {d.subject.nunique()} mice")
r13 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
r13["matches_paper"] = (r13.p < 0.05) == r13.paper_significant
print(r13.round(5).to_string(index=False))

Result: not reproduced. Five of the eight effects match the paper's pattern under both readings: baseline rate predicts HF frequency (p < 1e-5) and not HF ROV (p = 0.085); the EEG amplitude is predicted by HF frequency and LF ROV (p < 1e-5) and not LF frequency (p = 0.58 and 0.30). Baseline rate does not predict LF ROV (p = 0.65) and does predict LF frequency (p = 0.013 and 0.0035), and HF ROV does not predict the EEG (p = 0.96 and 0.92). The LF features rest on 4 mice and the EEG model on 262 trials from 3 mice.

figs13d-lf-crosscorrelation¶

Cross-correlation between LF thalamic units differs between rest and running, while that between HF units does not.

Per pair of units of the same group in a session (k-means split), in the late window: 2 ms bins of the absolute delays between their spikes on the same trial, divided by the number of seed spikes; the value is the mean of the first five bins (Methods). Rest and active per pair, signed-rank. Window (a) 150 to 250 ms or (b) 75 to 250 ms.

In [33]:
grp = hf_lf_groups("k-means (a)")
rows = []
for r in S.values():
    if not r.get("has_probes"):
        continue
    t = r["trials"]
    ok = ((t.intensity == "high") & t.is_valid).to_numpy()
    uid = r["units"].unit_id
    members = {}
    for i, (rel, trial) in r["spikes"].items():
        key = (r["subject"], int(uid.loc[i]))
        if key in grp.index:
            members.setdefault(grp.loc[key], []).append((rel, trial))
    for g, us in members.items():
        for wl, win in [("(a)", russo.LATE), ("(b)", russo.REBOUND)]:
            per = []
            for rel, trial in us:
                m = (rel >= win[0]) & (rel < win[1])
                per.append([rel[m & (trial == k)] for k in range(len(t))])
            for a in range(len(us)):
                for b in range(a + 1, len(us)):
                    v = {}
                    for st in ["rest", "active"]:
                        sel = ok & (t.active == (st == "active")).to_numpy()
                        idx = np.nonzero(sel)[0]
                        v[st] = russo.crosscorr_value([per[a][k] for k in idx], [per[b][k] for k in idx])
                    rows.append({"subject": r["subject"], "group": g, "window": wl, **v})
cc = pd.DataFrame(rows).dropna()
out = []
for (g, wl), d in cc.groupby(["group", "window"]):
    w = stats.wilcoxon(d.rest, d.active) if len(d) > 1 else None
    out.append({"group": g, "window": wl, "pairs": len(d), "mice": d.subject.nunique(), "rest_median": d.rest.median(),
                "active_median": d.active.median(), "rest_larger": int((d.rest > d.active).sum()), "p": w.pvalue if w else np.nan})
print(pd.DataFrame(out).round(5).to_string(index=False))

discussion-orthodromic-initial-excitation¶

The first-spike latency of the initial response is more variable in SM-TH than in MOs, and does not differ between SM-TH nuclei and TRN.

Per responsive unit at high intensity, the median and SD over trials of the first-spike latency in 3 to 50 ms. SM-TH are the relay units, MOs all responsive MOs units (RS and FS), TRN the thalamic units under 0.35 ms. Readings (criterion): (a) rank-sum on unit values; (b) signed-rank on per-mouse medians for mice with units in both groups.

                 "mice_1_larger": int((pm[g1] > pm[g2]).sum())})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(5).to_string(index=False))

# Variant: TRN also counts the units under 0.35 ms located in RT itself (TRN-RT)
d = H.copy()
d["grp"] = d.cls.replace({"relay": "SM-TH", "RS": "MOs", "FS": "MOs", "TRN-RT": "TRN"})
pu = d.groupby(["grp", "subject", "unit"]).lat_early.agg(["median", "std"]).reset_index()
a, b = pu[pu.grp == "SM-TH"]["median"].dropna(), pu[pu.grp == "TRN"]["median"].dropna()
pm = pu.groupby(["subject", "grp"])["median"].median().unstack()[["SM-TH", "TRN"]].dropna()
print(f"Latency, SM-TH relay against TRN with RT units: {len(a)} / {len(b)} units, medians {a.median() * 1e3:.2f} and "
      f"{b.median() * 1e3:.2f} ms, rank-sum p = {stats.mannwhitneyu(a, b).pvalue:.4f}; {len(pm)} mice, "
      f"signed-rank p = {stats.wilcoxon(pm['SM-TH'], pm['TRN']).pvalue:.4f}")

Latency, SM-TH relay against TRN with RT units: 301 / 19 units, medians 8.10 and 10.24 ms, rank-sum p = 0.0496; 6 mice, signed-rank p = 0.4375

Result: reproduced. The first-spike latency in 3 to 50 ms is more variable in SM-TH relay units than in MOs units (median SD 2.55 against 1.28 ms, rank-sum p < 1e-5; higher in 7 of 7 mice, p = 0.016), and the latency of SM-TH relay and TRN units does not differ (8.10 against 10.40 ms, p = 0.073; per mouse p = 0.44). With the RT unit added to TRN the rank-sum on units gives p = 0.0496 (8.10 against 10.24 ms) and the per-mouse test p = 0.44, so the claim holds under reading (b) with either TRN class.

source-data-link¶

The dandiset holds the mouse sessions behind the paper's Figure 1C and Figure 2B, so that values computed from it agree with the per-session and per-subject values in the paper's Source Data file.

No identifier links the Source Data rows to sessions, so the distributions are compared (criterion): the session count of Figure 1C (26 +- 3), its two medians (within 10%), and the five Figure 2B means (at least four within 10%), computed with the methods of fig1c and fig2b. The Source Data file is read from the publisher's site and checked against its SHA-256.

In [36]:
SOURCE_DATA_URL = ("https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41467-025-58717-2/"
                   "MediaObjects/41467_2025_58717_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx")
SOURCE_DATA_SHA256 = "5feebc5a6c6ced1441d0a74af35c7b18e1c2064f1e633f88c74ab0cd8689d0f7"
raw = requests.get(SOURCE_DATA_URL, timeout=120).content
print("Source Data SHA-256 matches:", hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() == SOURCE_DATA_SHA256, f"({len(raw)} bytes)")
xl = pd.ExcelFile(io.BytesIO(raw))


def paired_sheet(name):
    """Sheets with one value per subject: the two value columns below their header row."""
    d = pd.read_excel(xl, sheet_name=name, header=None)
    hdr = d.index[d.iloc[:, 1:].notna().sum(1) >= 2][0]
    cols = [c for c in d.columns[1:] if pd.notna(d.loc[hdr, c])]
    out = d.loc[hdr + 1:, cols].astype(float).dropna(how="all")
    out.columns = [str(d.loc[hdr, c]).strip() for c in cols]
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)


def box_sheet(name):
    """Box-plot sheets: for each block (title in row 1), rows are states and columns Min .. Max."""
    d = pd.read_excel(xl, sheet_name=name, header=None)
    out = {}
    titles = [(c, str(d.iloc[1, c])) for c in d.columns if pd.notna(d.iloc[1, c])]
    for c, title in titles:
        lab_col = c - 1
        rows = {}
        for i in range(5, len(d)):
            lab = d.iloc[i, lab_col]
            if pd.notna(lab):
                rows[str(lab).strip()] = d.iloc[i, c:c + 5].astype(float).to_numpy()
        out[title] = pd.DataFrame(rows, index=["min", "q25", "median", "q75", "max"]).T
    return out


sd1c = paired_sheet("Figure 1 C")
sd2b = pd.read_excel(xl, sheet_name="Figure 2 B", header=2).iloc[:, 1:]
print("Figure 1 C: %d pairs, medians rest %.1f, active %.1f uV" % (len(sd1c), sd1c.iloc[:, 0].median(), sd1c.iloc[:, 1].median()))
print("Figure 2 B: per-subject latencies, n and mean (ms):", {c: (int(sd2b[c].notna().sum()), round(sd2b[c].mean() * 1e3, 1)) for c in sd2b.columns})

    rows.append({"reading": label, "sessions": len(t), "rest_median": t.rest.median(), "active_median": t.active.median(),
                 "rest_vs_SD_%": 100 * (t.rest.median() / sd1c.iloc[:, 0].median() - 1),
                 "active_vs_SD_%": 100 * (t.active.median() / sd1c.iloc[:, 1].median() - 1)})
print("\nFigure 1C part:")
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(2).to_string(index=False))

# Figure 2B part: per mouse, mean latency over all high-intensity valid trials (both states)
per_mouse = {}
for r in S.values():
    if not r.get("has_probes"):
        continue
    t = r["trials"]
    hi = ((t.intensity == "high") & t.is_valid).to_numpy()
    vals = {"EEG (s)": np.nanmean(r["eeg_lat"][hi]), "LFP (s)": np.nanmean(r["lfp_lat"][hi]), "CSD (s)": np.nanmean(r["csd_lat"][hi])}
    for name, cls in [("SM-TH (s)", "relay"), ("MOs (s)", "RS")]:
        s = trial_unit_latency(cls)
        if r["subject"] in s.index.get_level_values(0):
            v = s.loc[r["subject"]].reindex(range(len(t)))[hi]
            vals[name] = v.mean()
    per_mouse[r["subject"]] = vals
pm2b = pd.DataFrame(per_mouse).T
cmp = pd.DataFrame({"mice": pm2b.notna().sum(), "this_mean_ms": pm2b.mean() * 1e3, "SD_n": sd2b.notna().sum(),
                    "SD_mean_ms": sd2b.mean() * 1e3})
cmp["diff_%"] = 100 * (cmp.this_mean_ms / cmp.SD_mean_ms - 1)

The Figure 1C part does not: the dandiset holds 10 deep MOs sessions (20 with high and medium), against 26 in the Source Data, and the medians are 16.5% (rest) and 37.2% (active) below the Source Data medians at high intensity.

Human claims on the Source Data file¶

The human recordings are not public. The claims below are tested, as their criteria say, on the per-subject values or box-plot summaries in the paper's Source Data file (data: elsewhere).

fig1a-tms-late-rest-active¶

In 12 healthy subjects, the late (150 to 250 ms) TMS-evoked EEG response over premotor channels has a larger rectified amplitude and phase locking at rest than during active hand squeezing (amplitude 1.37 +- 0.59 against 0.77 +- 0.22 uV; PLF 0.21 +- 0.07 against 0.15 +- 0.05).

In [37]:
a1 = paired_sheet("Figure 1 A")
rest, act = a1.iloc[:, 0], a1.iloc[:, 1]
w = stats.wilcoxon(rest, act)
print(f"Figure 1 A: {len(a1)} subjects; rest {rest.mean():.3f} +- {rest.std():.3f} uV, active {act.mean():.3f} +- {act.std():.3f} uV; "
      f"rest larger in {int((rest > act).sum())}; two-sided signed-rank p = {w.pvalue:.4g} (paper 0.002)")
print(f"Within tolerance: rest |{rest.mean():.3f} - 1.37| <= 0.59: {abs(rest.mean() - 1.37) <= 0.59}; "
      f"active |{act.mean():.3f} - 0.77| <= 0.22: {abs(act.mean() - 0.77) <= 0.22}")
s1a = box_sheet("Figure S1A")
for k, v in s1a.items():
    print(f"\nFigure S1A, {k}:")
    print(v.to_string())

fig1b-ieeg-late-rest-active¶

In 5 epilepsy patients, the late (150 to 250 ms) iEEG response to single-pulse electrical stimulation of premotor cortex is smaller in rectified amplitude and PLF during active hand squeezing than at rest.

figs2-tms-controls¶

The TMS late-component modulation is also seen with passive hand movement and with leg cycling, is absent for posterior TMS, is absent for median nerve somatosensory evoked potentials, and does not differ between hand closing and opening.

Result: reproduced, as far as the public data allow. The early amplitude median is 2.15 uV at rest and 1.75 uV active, each within the paper's mean and SD; the early PLF medians are 0.41 and 0.40. The tests and the correlation cannot be recomputed from box-plot summaries.

figs3b-ieeg-early-no-modulation¶

The early (3 to 50 ms) iEEG response to electrical stimulation in humans is not modulated by state, in monopolar or bipolar derivation.

Result: reproduced, on a test that cannot find an effect. None of the four signed-rank tests on the five subjects gives p < 0.05 (p = 0.31 to 0.88), and the per-subject differences are small and of mixed sign (-0.08 to +0.09). With five pairs the smallest possible p is 0.0625.

Model claims (fig4e, fig4f, fig4hi, figs14a, figs14b)¶

The criteria ask for a rerun of the paper's model, the stim branch of github.com/bazhlab-ucsd/sleep-stage-transition (commit 76ea885), with the analysis code on figshare (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.25773501.v1, MATLAB). The Methods (Thalamocortical network model) give the two states: rest as the parameters were tuned, active with the CX to TC and CX to RE miniEPSPs raised from 30 to 50 and the thalamic acetylcholine level lowered from 1.3 to 1; 30 trials of 15 s (15 rest, 15 active), the pulse at 8 to 9.75 s in steps of 125 ms. The cell below fetches the model at the commit, builds it in a temporary directory with the Makefile, and times 200 ms of simulation of the published network, to estimate what the 30 trials cost on this runner (4 CPUs).

In [42]:
import os
import subprocess
import tarfile
import tempfile

MODEL_REPO = "bazhlab-ucsd/sleep-stage-transition"   # branch stim, the paper's model (claims file)
MODEL_COMMIT = "76ea8853fa4e97ac8c47032bc00f378a0920f9d0"
TEST_MS = 200                                         # simulated time of each timing run


def set_params(text, **kw):
    lines = [(f"{k.split()[0]} {kw[k.split()[0]]}" if k.strip() and k.split()[0] in kw else k) for k in text.splitlines()]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    tgz = requests.get(f"https://codeload.github.com/{MODEL_REPO}/tar.gz/{MODEL_COMMIT}", timeout=300).content
    tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(tgz)).extractall(tmp, filter="data")
    src = os.path.join(tmp, os.listdir(tmp)[0])
    params = open(os.path.join(src, "params.txt")).read()
    keys = ["tmax", "num_mp_threads", "stim_cx_start", "stim_cx_end", "stim_cx_strength", "stim_cx_start_neuron",
            "stim_cx_end_neuron", "stim_in_start_neuron", "stim_in_end_neuron", "ach_cx_awake", "ach_th_awake"]
    print(f"{MODEL_REPO} at {MODEL_COMMIT[:7]}: the parameter set in params.txt")
    print({l.split()[0]: l.split()[1] for l in params.splitlines() if l.strip() and l.split()[0] in keys})
    print("CX to TC and CX to RE AMPA_D2 lines of network.cfg (Mini_s is the miniEPSP strength):")
    for l in open(os.path.join(src, "network.cfg")).read().splitlines():
        if l.split()[:3] in (["CX", "TC", "AMPA_D2"], ["CX", "RE", "AMPA_D2"]):
            print("  " + l.strip())
    t0 = time.time()
    for cmd in (["make", "-s", "mindcurrent"], ["make", "-s", "network"]):
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=src, capture_output=True, text=True)
        print(" ".join(cmd), "exit", r.returncode)
    with open(os.path.join(src, "connection_info2"), "w") as fh:
        subprocess.run(["./generate_network", "network.cfg"], cwd=src, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True)
    print(f"built the model and its network in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
    speed = {}
    for threads in [1, 4]:
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(src, f"run{threads}"))
        with open(os.path.join(src, f"run{threads}", "params.txt"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write(set_params(params, tmax=TEST_MS, num_mp_threads=threads))
        t0 = time.time()
        subprocess.run(["./mindcurrent", f"run{threads}/params.txt", f"run{threads}", "connection_info2"], cwd=src,
                       capture_output=True, check=True)
        speed[threads] = (time.time() - t0) / (TEST_MS / 1000)
        print(f"{threads} thread(s): {TEST_MS} ms simulated in {time.time() - t0:.1f} s, "
              f"{speed[threads]:.0f} s per simulated second")

# Methods: 30 trials (15 rest, 15 active), pulse at 8 to 9.75 s in steps of 125 ms, trials of 15 s
pulses = 8.0 + 0.125 * np.arange(15)
sim_min = 2 * (pulses + 0.25).sum()        # each trial simulated only to 250 ms after its pulse
sim_full = 30 * 15.0
for label, s in [("to 250 ms after each pulse", sim_min), ("15 s trials (Methods)", sim_full)]:
    print(f"30 trials {label}: {s:.0f} s simulated; four single-thread runs at once "
          f"{s * speed[1] / 4 / 3600:.1f} h, one four-thread run {s * speed[4] / 3600:.1f} h")
print("Notebook limit 1 h (docs/protocol.md); fig4hi-model-gaba-contributions adds runs with TRN silenced, "
      "IN silenced and a grid of GABA-A strengths")

Blocked (not_runnable). The model builds and runs: one parameter set ships with the branch (the rest state: thalamic acetylcholine 1.3, CX to TC and CX to RE miniEPSP strength 30), and the active state is a change of three values the Methods give. The obstacle is time: on this runner one simulated second takes about 120 s on one thread and 80 s on four (cell above; the timing varies between runs: 121 to 123 s and 82 to 83 s in the three runs of the last revision, 158 s and 113 s in an earlier run). The 30 trials of fig4e, fig4f, figs14a and figs14b need 274 s of simulation even when each trial stops 250 ms after its pulse (450 s for the Methods' 15 s trials), about 2.3 h with four single-thread runs at once (3.8 h for 15 s trials), against the notebook's one-hour limit; fig4hi adds runs with TRN silenced, with IN silenced and over a grid of GABA-A strengths. The analysis code is MATLAB and was not ported.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The dandiset holds 10 of the paper's mouse sessions with deep MOs stimulation (the paper: 26 EEG sessions from 15 mice, units from 21 mice), so every mouse test has fewer animals. Bad channels and trials were removed in the paper by visual inspection and a lab spreadsheet; here all channels and trials, and the file's own is_data_valid and is_valid flags, are both shown. Responsive units use 10 ms bins in place of the paper's adaptive kernel. The dip test uses the diptest package. The CSD averages the two sites of each Neuropixels row. The rest against running rate tests of fig3a and figs10a are shown also within sessions (van Elteren), as pooling trials over sessions mixes sessions with different rates and fractions of active trials. The HF and LF groups are a k-means split with 18 LF units (8 at the paper's 17.88 ms), so every HF and LF claim is tested on groups unlike the paper's 569 HF and 700 LF units. The model claims were built and timed, not run. The human claims use the per-subject values and box-plot summaries of the Source Data file, as their criteria say.

What was found about the dataset. The units' waveform_duration is described as seconds and holds milliseconds. The trial table's is_running uses a 0 cm/s threshold, not the paper's 0.1 cm/s. No session has stimulation of the posterior control areas of Figure S6. The EEG, LFP, units and trial table share a clock: in the trial-averaged raw signals the stimulation artifact sits within 0.2 ms of the trial onset in the EEG and within 0.6 ms (1.5 samples) in the LFP of every session, and units fire in 2 to 10 ms after the pulse in every mouse. The relay units' evoked ISIs are unimodal here (median 2.6 ms), with few units above the paper's 17.88 ms threshold, so the HF and LF split of the paper's Figure 3 cannot be recovered from this subset.
